prompt: This should print `adult` only when `age` is 18 or more. Which line is wrong?
Which operator tests whether two values are equal? Type it.
explain: `==` compares, `=` assigns. Writing `=` inside an `if` is a classic bug.
A single `=` assigns: it puts 5 into `n`, and the value of that assignment (5) counts as true. To compare you need `==`. Most compilers warn about this mistake, so read warnings.

C has no separate true/false printing here: a comparison gives the number 1 when it is true and 0 when it is false. 8 % 2 is 0, so `0 == 0` is true and prints 1. That is why `return n % 2 == 0;` works for `is_even`.
